analysis.title: "No Offense Being Played": Hedge Funds Add Gross, Cut Nets As CTAs Hit "Target" And Buybacks Go Dark
key_insights: Goldman prime book: gross leverage rose 0.7 pts to 308.7% (60th percentile 1-year) while net leverage fell 1.5 pts to 75.9% (10th percentile). L/S ratio fell 1.2% to 1.652 (14th percentile).

Fundamental L/S funds raised gross 3.3 pts to 209.5% (43rd percentile) while net slipped 0.2 pts to 52.9% (6th percentile). Goldman's Saboureault says there is 'no offense being played' by fundamental funds, who are uncomfortable with indices near record highs.

US L/S gross rose 3.8 pts to 213% (53rd percentile). US L/S net rose 0.5 pts, the first rise in four weeks, to 46.9% (2nd percentile 1-year). The US fundamental long/short ratio fell to 1.565, the 1st percentile on a five-year basis.

Short sales outpaced long buys 1.3 to 1 and global equities were net sold for the week (-0.3 SDs). The GS Fundamental L/S estimate fell 0.70% from 10/2 to 10/8 while MSCI World rose 0.78%, driven by losses on both long and short sides. Systematic L/S funds gained 0.82%.

Info Tech went from the most net bought US sector in 4 of the past 5 weeks to by far the most net sold this week (-1.0 SDs 1-year), driven by long and short sales. Saboureault attributes the trigger to OpenAI revenue headlines, which set off selling in Semis/Tech.

Hedge funds were reported to be the most overweight the Magnificent 7 on record as of Friday, and tech's share of total US exposure has been rebuilt almost back to its summer multi-year high. AI vs everything else hit a record 10-point gap in five weeks, and Goldman is telling clients to start buying the losers.

Hedge funds cut US Health Care risk for a 4th straight week. Since mid-August Biotech has seen the largest dollar de-grossing of any US subsector, and its trailing 8-week de-grossing is the largest in more than five years.

US Industrials were net bought at the fastest pace since early January (+1.8 SDs), almost entirely long buys, after 5 straight weeks of selling. Aerospace & Defense, Construction & Engineering, Airlines and Industrial Conglomerates led. Consumer Discretionary, Financials and Real Estate were also bought. Info Tech, Materials, Staples and Comm Svcs were sold.
Staples were net sold for a 3rd straight week (7 of the last 8), entirely via short sales. The article links this to rising rates offering a risk-free return above the sector's dividend yield.

US-listed ETF shorts rose 4.4% on the week (+6.2% month-over-month), led by Large Cap Equity and Tech ETFs. Europe saw risk-on flows for a 3rd consecutive week, and Goldman's book is 2.41% overweight Europe vs MSCI World and 17.39% underweight North America.

Asset managers finished the week as small net sellers per Goldman's desk. CFTC data showed institutions as small net buyers of S&P futures in the week ending Sept 29. Non-dealer index futures net length is $282bn, vs a long-term average of $85bn and a $342bn peak.

EPFR: global equity funds took in $12.4bn last week after a $15.8bn outflow the prior week. US funds took in $3.3bn and Japan funds saw $3.3bn of selling. Retail had two of its lowest (still positive) imbalance days since early August.

Goldman's model puts CTAs long about $43.5bn of global equities, down from $125bn a month ago and $67bn last week, roughly $81bn of selling or two-thirds of their length. The selling was largely global, presumably Korea's Kospi, while US CTA exposure is flat near $40bn.

Saboureault says CTAs are virtually 'on target' with no significant flow expected unless a clearer trend appears. In a flat tape CTAs sell $3.6bn globally next week but buy $5.3bn in the US, where all modeled SPX and NDX trend signals remain positive. Over a month a flat tape means $6bn of buying.
CTA flows are large in both directions: a large up move over the next month brings $137bn of buying, a large down move brings $144bn of selling, $66bn of it in the US.
S&P pivot levels are 7,704 (short term), 7,493 (medium term, the most important) and 7,012 (long term). With the index at 7,811 on Friday, the short-term trigger is 1.4% away.

Corporate buyback desk flows are 0.8x 2025 YTD ADTV, concentrated in Financials, Health Care and Energy, with 10b5-1 plans at 86% of desk volume vs 14% discretionary. Goldman expects corporates to exit blackout 1-2 days after reporting, with about 10% of the S&P in the open window by Friday vs about 7% now, followed by an inflection in repurchase volumes.
North America IPOs and follow-ons were $2.66bn last week, bringing the YTD total to $512bn.

Sentiment: AAII bulls rose 5.7 pts to 40.3% and bears fell 7.5 pts to 39.0% (spread 1.3) in the week ending Oct 7. CNN Fear & Greed rose to 45 from 43. Goldman's US Equity Sentiment Indicator edged up to -0.7 from -0.9, still negative.

Breadth: the median S&P 500 stock trades 16% below its 52-week high, the weakest breadth since the Dot-Com Bubble. One-month S&P implied correlation is 10.2% vs a record low of 7.0% and a long-term average of 29%. A Goldman partner found 10 stocks driving 68% of Q3 earnings growth.
Goldman's Risk Appetite Indicator fell from around 1.0 in August to 0.1, below its long-term average of 0.4.
S&P put skew (1.13) is below its 1.16 average while call skew (0.88) is above its 0.83 average, so there is little demand for crash protection while upside calls are bid.
S&P e-mini top-of-book depth rebounded to $16.35mm, above its $11.5mm average. Funding spreads are 73bps vs a 52bps long-run average, well below the summer peak of 118bps.
The week ahead: bank earnings from Tuesday, ASML Wednesday and TSMC Thursday, US CPI Wednesday, then PPI, Retail Sales, Philly Fed and a Warsh speech at the IMF on Thursday.

Saboureault's bull case: CTAs are on target, buybacks have slowed and the retail bid is hesitant, but there is no shortage of potential marginal buyers if the oil and rates overhangs recede. The article's author argues the market likely has to get through oil and rates before 8,000, and that the 7,704 CTA trigger is closer than either.

tension_points.bull_case: Fundamental net leverage is at the 6th percentile, the US L/S ratio is at a five-year low, CTAs are flushed and buybacks are about to return, so there are many potential marginal buyers if oil and rates overhangs recede.
tension_points.bear_case: Oil is exposed to Middle East conflict and rates to a hawkish Warsh Fed, with CPI Wednesday and a Warsh speech Thursday. Breadth is at Dot-Com lows and implied correlation near record lows.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break of the 7,704 short-term S&P CTA trigger, with 7,493 as the medium-term pivot, would invalidate the bull case.
